generation.explanation: The matrix M = [[2,1],[0,1]] sends every point (x, y) to (2x + y, y) — a horizontal stretch by 2 combined with a shear. Its columns are exactly the images of the basis vectors: î lands on (2, 0) and ĵ lands on (1, 1), so the unit square becomes a parallelogram. The determinant det(M) = 2·1 − 1·0 = 2 tells you that every area doubles: the unit square (area 1) becomes a parallelogram of area 2. Use the slider to morph between the identity and M, and drag the orange point v to see where M takes it!
